content.thinking:
I'm planning the bookshelf module's overall dimensions and structure, setting up a root joint and designing the frame parts to build out from there.

I'm working out the proportions for posts, shelves, back panel, and a decorative arched crest on top, sketching coordinates for each piece before writing the box and extrude geometry calls that will generate them, along with gold moon and star decal shapes.

Writing shape geometry...

I confirm the winding is consistent, forming a simple crescent polygon with CCW outer arc and CW inner arc back to start. Now I'm shifting to designing standing books: defining a function that draws a cover box, inset cream pages, and spine detail for each book, facing front to show its spine.

For the spine construction, I'm working out the geometry — spine board at the front, thin cover sides, and a cream page block in between — and considering using a shared set of textured spine decals to avoid generating a unique SVG per book.

Adding a cream page strip on top and thinking through how lying/stacked books differ from upright ones -- covers top and bottom, pages peeking out front, spine along one side, so I need separate geometry logic for horizontal book placement.

I'll add a gold clasp box at the front center of the cover, then build the orb stands with lathe-based bases, leg rods, and a crescent piece. For the orbs themselves, I'm using glowing purple spheres with a small white highlight sphere for sheen and a gold ring band, plus a third pale sphere for the armillary.

For the armillary sphere I'm crossing three gold tori with a stand and central sphere. Candlesticks get a lathe-turned gold base, a cream wax cylinder with drips, and a glowing teardrop-shaped flame with a dark wick box and wax ring on top. The scrolls are horizontal cream cylinders with darker spiral end caps, tied with red torus ribbons, gold seal discs, and tassels, stacked in a pyramid of three.

Now I'm detailing the potion bottle with a lathe-turned blue glowing outline, gold cork collar, and cork stopper with a subtle glow strength. For the hanging charms I'm adding a gold crescent moon on a chain and a glowing blue crystal octahedron on the left post, and a lantern with a purple tassel on the right, using thin gold rods as chains and skipping extra joint detail. I'm also adding gold cap boxes with spiked finials atop the posts, a star plaque on the post front, gold banding, bottom foot blocks with diamonds, and small inner finials, then applying a dark indigo wood grain texture to wrap the posts.

Writing wood grain shaders...

I'll skip the risky arc sweep and instead add a thin gold crescent using a catmull curve path swept with a small radius, keeping it simple. Then I'm planning the floor items, starting with a stack of books positioned front-left on the floor, outside the shelf's footprint.

Now I'm working out the precise vertical coordinates for the shelf structure: board centers and tops for each of the three shelf levels, the resulting bay heights, and the post height reaching up to y=1.5, making sure everything sits correctly with nothing dipping below the floor plane.

Still working out finials, posts, shelf boards, and back panel dimensions, then starting to outline the crest shape with its peak coordinates.

Adjusting crest decoration depths so the gold ring, crescent, and star sit flush against the wood front face without gaps, tweaking thickness and z-offsets accordingly.

Checking the extrude orientation to confirm the thickness axis runs along +z so the front face lands correctly, then starting to define the gold star's outline points.

Writing helper functions for star and crescent shapes, working through winding order and orientation flips to avoid faces pointing the wrong way...

Now I'm detailing post decorations: gold diamond plaques on the front faces, gold band boxes wrapped around the posts, and gold-framed dark blue feet at the base matching the reference design.

Then I'm positioning the post vertically from the foot up to full height, and establishing z-depth coordinates for the shelf items—keeping them centered within the bay depth, clear of the back panel. I'm starting to lay out bay 1's items from the left edge.

For bay 1, I'm arranging scrolls, three standing colored books, a potion bottle, a stack of books, and an armillary sphere left to right along the shelf. Bay 2 gets its own arrangement with an armillary piece, leaning books, a horizontal book stack with an orb stand, and two candles spaced apart for clearance, and I'm starting on bay 3's layout with a smaller astrolabe-like piece.

Now I'm designing the book-building function, where each book is a box with a cover color and spine decal plane positioned just in front of the body to add detail.

Still designing spine textures...

Still writing SVG colors...

Still shaping the orb stand geometry...

Adding splayed gold legs...

For the orb itself I'll keep it simple: a glowing sphere with a highlight, skipping fancy swirl textures since paint and glow don't mix well. Then I'll add the armillary sphere effect with three gold torus rings oriented differently—one equatorial and two meridian rings at different rotations—to encircle the orb.

For the candle stands, I'm working out a lathe profile for the gold base with a pedestal shape, then adding a cylindrical candle on top.

Adding wax drip and flame details...

Adding darker inner spiral discs and gold cap cylinders poking out each end of the scroll rods for a finished handle look.

I'm wrapping a red ribbon torus around the scroll and adding a gold wax seal disc plus a hanging tassel with a bead, then arranging rolls into a stacked bundle positioned along the x-axis with rolls offset in z.

For the potion bottle, I'm lathing a flask-shaped outline with a deep blue glass color, adding a gold collar and brown cork, and topping it with a small gold star label on the front face.

I'm placing a gold astrolabe with torus rings and stand in bay 3, positioning it left of the books, then working out a hanging crescent charm on a gold chain from the left post.

Adding more charms...

Still placing finial pieces...

I'm picking slightly bluer wood tones for the posts and back panel versus the main shelves. For floor books, I want a stack with one lying at an angle, but my current builder doesn't support rotation directly, so I'm sketching a helper that converts local coordinates into placed positions to fake a rotated transform.

Writing coordinate transform logic...

I'm picking gold and shading colors, deciding to use flat colors for small gold bits and cel-shaded paint for larger surfaces to keep texel density manageable, and building out the flat color palette for ribbons, cords, flames, glass, orbs, and other small details.

For the book spine decals, I'm working out how to orient a plane to face the correct direction on tilted, rotated books by computing rotation from the transform, then sketching a helper function to place box geometry with position and rotation derived from a transform object, while checking what the Fill type export looks like in the context module.

For cylinders rolled along different axes, I need to compose quaternions properly—combining a base orientation quaternion with a local rotation quaternion so the geometry orients correctly regardless of which axis it rolls around.

Still building quaternion math...

Working through extrude/lathe direction vectors for rotated geometry...

For lathes like potions and candle holders, yaw doesn't matter since they're upright, so I'll just handle them directly at their world position. Now I need to plan the imports carefully to avoid unused variable errors under strict typechecking -- THREE, builder helper, outline point type, svg, glow, cel, grain, paint, and skip anything unused like mix or shadowOf.

Writing imports and type definitions...

Now I'm defining the texture generator for the spine, picking an emblem shape (star, moon, or diamond) and building the SVG path for it with a gold accent color.

Adding decorative bands and the moon emblem shape...

Working out both arcs pass on the left side, giving a crescent with a shallower bulge and openings facing right. Now I'm setting up a spine texture mapping structure, pairing colors with symbols like star and moon.

Building the upright book function...

Still writing book geometry...

Adjusting the clasp plate position onto the pages inset and skipping the tassel and top emblem for simplicity. I'll set up a transform helper for placing items without rotation, then work through shelf geometry—defining bay floor data and a center depth for items so books and objects sit consistently within the shelf's front-to-back range.

For bay one I'm placing the scroll stack, a row of upright books with slight width and height variation, a potion bottle, and then a stack of lying books ordered purple-green-red from top to bottom with small vertical offsets between each.

I'm figuring out small yaw variations for the lying books for natural variance, and checking that the armillary sphere at x=0.58 with radius 0.07 doesn't collide with the side post, adjusting its radius down to 0.06 so it clears the shelf boundary. Now I'm moving to bay two and placing its armillary sphere near x=-0.56.

Still placing bay 2 objects...

Now moving to bay 3 at y0=1.04, positioning the astrolabe at x=-0.57 and starting on the book stack placements there.

I'm also working out whether to tilt one of the books to lean against its neighbor, calculating the rotation direction needed so the top edge sways toward +x and rests against the green book rather than away from it.

Then I'm placing the remaining objects: the purple orb on its stand, the stacked scrolls, and a tall candle on a pedestal at the far right matching the reference image's top shelf. For the floor level, I'm positioning the big blue book lying flat with a slight rotation, with a red book stacked underneath it to match the reference's layered book pile.

Next, I'm adjusting the scroll resting in front of the books, rotating it along its length and nudging its position so the footprint fits within the shelf depth, settling on z-centers around 0.38 for the books and 0.54 for the scroll to keep the composition balanced.

Now I'm defining a scroll-building function: cylinders for the paper body and a darker inner layer, a gold knob cap, and small torus shapes for the tie bindings wrapped around the roll.

Then I'm assembling a stack of three scrolls plus a sealing wax disc and a hanging tassel spike to finish the composition.

For the orb stand, I'm building a lathe-generated base shape from an outline profile, giving it a gold color and defined segment count for a smooth rounded form.

I'm now computing where to place a horizontal ring torus on the orb, working out the ring's position and radius so it sits tangent to the sphere surface at the correct height using the sphere's center and radius geometry.

For the crescent moon accent, I'm sketching a simpler approach: instead of a full curved sweep, I'll add three small gold cone "claws" positioned around the ring and tilted outward to suggest the horns of a crescent, looping through their angular positions to place each one.

Then I'm planning the holder's legs as three gold rods angling from a mid-height ring down to a wider base near the ground, followed by the orb sphere itself with a soft glow, a small white highlight for shine, and a couple of lighter embedded patches on its surface to give it a swirled texture.

Now I'm sketching out an armillary sphere variant: a lathed stand and stem rising to a ring center, with multiple tilted torus rings representing orbital bands around a central sphere, using rotation offsets to angle each ring differently.

I'm also planning an astrolabe model: a stand and stem supporting concentric torus rings and a dark indigo disc face, with a gold cross-rod and star shape extruded at the center to decorate the instrument.

I'm adding tick marks around the disc edge using small gold boxes rotated radially at intervals, then moving on to a candle piece with pedestal, body, and flame geometry that glows, plus hanging charm posts and shelf back-panel details.

I'm skipping dust and cobweb effects, keeping book spine textures small for the atlas, and placing a handful of gold constellation stars flush against the back panel in the gaps between shelf items.

I'm scattering a few more small decorations—stars, a purple orb, a moon—around the bays near the books and candles, then tallying up the total part count across books, scrolls, orbs, candles, and posts to roughly 350.

Writing build function...

Refining helper signature for texture support...

Now I'm sketching small factory helpers: a transform-at builder, geometry shorthand functions for boxes/cylinders/spheres/toruses, and a star outline point generator for decorative shapes.

Writing extrude function...

Now I'm defining the crescent moon outline, computing points along an outer arc from 51.3° sweeping around, then planning an inner arc for the concave edge.

I'll drop the flip parameter since winding direction shouldn't cause issues, and the sharp crescent tips can just use default smoothing. Now I'm setting up the moon function similarly to the star function, then moving into the wood paint definitions for the post and shelf materials.

Adding plank paint logic...

Still placing post details...

Still placing cap elements and cornice geometry...

Working out the base apron shape between the feet, extruding a curved profile along the front using the wood post color, with the outline tapering between the leg positions.

I'm also placing a small gold decorative arc and star above the apron, positioning them at slightly offset z-depths so they sit just in front of the apron surface.

For the back panel, I'm using a planked background box sized to fill the space between the bottom shelf and the top, then adding a crest piece extruded from an outline at the top, colored to match the wood post with slight smoothing.

Mapping out the crest outline points now, starting from the bottom-left sharp corner and curving up through the arched top, with concave dips near the shoulders that should flow smoothly given the smoothing setting. Now adding a gold trim sweep along the top edge of the crest.

Still computing trim curve points...

Working out the star placement inside the crescent opening, then positioning smaller decorative stars symmetrically on either side of the crest while checking they stay clear of the trim boundary.

Now I'm adding the ring's torus geometry, mini gold cone finials with dark base blocks positioned near the crest, and setting up the chain attachment points for the charms on each post.

Writing chain rod code...

For the moon charm, I'm figuring out placement at the post's front-left corner so it hangs naturally in front of the post rather than overlapping it.

Positioning the moon charm on the left post slightly in front of the panel so it reads clearly, and placing the crystal chain beside it; the lantern goes on the right post with similar front offset, checking it clears the shelf boards. For attachment, I'm adding small gold hook spheres with short rods connecting each charm back to the post band.

Still placing lantern geometry...

Now I'm defining a candle-building helper function that generates the stand, wax cylinder, and related geometry for each candle placement.

Defining the flame outline points and the candle stand profile for the lathe geometry...

Finishing the pedestal outline, I decide to skip the small gold ring and star plaque details to keep the stem simple, then verify bay heights stay under 1.0 by adding up pedestal, candle, and flame dimensions for each bay.

I'm checking orb and potion proportions, then double-checking the builder API signatures for rod, spike, and lathe to make sure parameters like radius, direction, and segment count line up correctly before finalizing the structure.

Now I'm defining helper types for outline points and cone geometry, then mapping out texture keys for the book covers so each color variant has a consistent naming scheme.

I'm positioning the books and scroll stack within the first bay, carefully spacing widths and centers so covers don't overlap and gaps stay visually consistent.

Next I'm placing the potion, the lying stack at x=0.30, and the armillary sphere at 0.575, then returning to detail the scroll stack itself—defining individual rolled scrolls with varying lengths, offsets, and tie positions so they read as a loose pile rather than uniform cylinders.

I'm also adding a wax seal with a hanging tassel on the front roll, parameterizing the scroll function to accept tie positions as an array, and reusing that same scroll stack at a second bay location, plus placing one scroll on the floor with a seal but skipping the tassel there to keep it simpler.

I'm skipping texture details for the lying book and back stars since they're minor, setting up a flat gold cel color for seals, and making sure the flat rendering option passes through correctly as an optional boolean. Now I'm finalizing the spine plane positioning for the upright book accounting for its rotation, then writing out the complete code.
